Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses item embedding geometry and positive–negative score separation. Model architecture is not shown. It accesses `item_emb.weight`, computes per-position sequence features through `log2feats(sequence)`, and scores candidate items with `predict_score(features, items)`. It does not explicitly extract or inspect a final user representation; how sequence features are constructed depends on the model implementation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` expects the model or compatibility view to expose `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Reviews and histories are stored but unused by these probes.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. Up to ten batches are evaluated without gradients, with the model in evaluation mode. Positive and negative candidates are stacked into `B × L × 2`; positions with positive item ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`**: Samples up to 2,048 non-padding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result through `(mean_cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment and possible collapse; approximately orthogonal embeddings score around 0.5.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`**: Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive minus negative logits. Larger values indicate stronger separation, including among difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`**: Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`**: Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`**: Counts low-margin and wrong-ranking positions and lists the twenty most frequent metadata categories separately for positive and negative items. These are raw counts, not exposure-normalized failure rates.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, substitution, or sensitivity tests occur. Random embedding subsampling and loader-provided negative candidates are the only sampling mechanisms.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. A separate interpreter prompt requests a JSON assessment containing `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; this interpretation is not generated by the probe itself.

The probes measure training-pair separation, not validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, or recommendation diversity. Margins depend on logit scale and negative sampling. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty. No review information or simulator traits are measured. Empty margin samples return zeros, which can misleadingly resemble healthy error rates.

[CoDeR (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379) models demand shifts amid noisy histories; its causal interpretation depends on its assumptions. [Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360802500070X) warns that random cropping, masking, and reordering can change sequence semantics.

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: mask recent events, remove repeated-interest evidence, and shuffle order as separate interventions. Define repeated interests using observable item recurrence or title/description similarity; these are proxies, not observed intent. Compare targeted removals against equal-size random removals matched on position and item popularity where feasible; preserve the item multiset for order probes, and distinguish shuffling older context from moving the latest item. and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses item embedding geometry and positive–negative score separation. Model architecture is not shown. It accesses `item_emb.weight`, computes per-position sequence features through `log2feats(sequence)`, and scores candidate items with `predict_score(features, items)`. It does not explicitly extract or inspect a final user representation; how sequence features are constructed depends on the model implementation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` expects the model or compatibility view to expose `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Reviews and histories are stored but unused by these probes.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. Up to ten batches are evaluated without gradients, with the model in evaluation mode. Positive and negative candidates are stacked into `B × L × 2`; positions with positive item ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`**: Samples up to 2,048 non-padding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result through `(mean_cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment and possible collapse; approximately orthogonal embeddings score around 0.5.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`**: Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive minus negative logits. Larger values indicate stronger separation, including among difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`**: Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`**: Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`**: Counts low-margin and wrong-ranking positions and lists the twenty most frequent metadata categories separately for positive and negative items. These are raw counts, not exposure-normalized failure rates.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, substitution, or sensitivity tests occur. Random embedding subsampling and loader-provided negative candidates are the only sampling mechanisms.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. A separate interpreter prompt requests a JSON assessment containing `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; this interpretation is not generated by the probe itself.

The probes measure training-pair separation, not validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, or recommendation diversity. Margins depend on logit scale and negative sampling. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty. No review information or simulator traits are measured. Empty margin samples return zeros, which can misleadingly resemble healthy error rates.
